$comment: Declared skill-listing surface. Enforced by scripts/skill-surface.test.mjs, which runs
under `npm test`. Deliberately NOT enforced by hooks/pre-commit: that hook is not wired
into .git/hooks (issue #115), so a check placed there would never execute.
Why this file exists: plugin installs live in ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json,
which is machine-local and has no repo representation. Without a committed declaration
there is nothing to diff and nothing to fail, so cleanup silently regresses. Changing the
surface means editing this file in the same commit -- a deliberate, reviewable act.
Claude Code loads every skill name+description into context. The budget is 1% of the
model context window; on overflow it drops descriptions starting with the LEAST-invoked
skills, so rarely-used skills lose their trigger keywords and become harder to invoke,
which keeps them at the front of the drop queue. Overlap evicts your own skills.
The target this file enforces toward is written up in docs/reference/skill-surface-standard.md.
BLAST RADIUS. This file carries SIX top-level blocks -- plugins, localSkills, references,
entryPoints, catalogOnly, overlapVerdicts -- and FOUR test files read it (counted 2026-08-11
by grepping the repo for `readPolicy`): scripts/skill-surface.test.mjs, which owns SHAPE
validation for every block; scripts/graph-integrity.test.mjs; scripts/reference-integrity
.test.mjs; and scripts/graph-integrity.overlap.test.mjs. It is parsed as one document, so a
malformed edit anywhere -- a trailing comma, an unescaped quote -- fails all four at once,
not the block you were editing. Add a block only alongside the test that consumes it.

plugins.$comment: Expected plugin -> install scope. Any drift in either direction fails the check.

The local record was a duplicate enable in template-image-generator that registry.md had claimed was purged on 2026-06-18; it never was, and declaring the observed state as expected turned a known defect into policy. Removed via the casing fix below. They are NOT in the `removed` set -- the plugin itself is still wanted at user scope, and `removed` is keyed by plugin name, so listing one there would fail the resurrection check against its own legitimate install.

$casing-hazard: ROOT CAUSE of the repeated superpowers/feature-dev returns, diagnosed 2026-08-06.
`claude plugin uninstall --scope local|project` matches the stored `projectPath` against
`process.cwd()` with a CASE-SENSITIVE compare. Node reports `C:\Users\...` while older
records were written as `c:\Users\...`, so the lookup misses and the CLI reports the
plugin is 'not installed in local scope' -- from the correct directory. Fix: correct the
casing in the record, then let the CLI do the removal.
The same bug keys one directory as two projects: marketing-skills briefly had TWO project
records, written by the CLI itself 35 seconds apart, differing only in that first character.
Two earlier purges appeared to 'not stick'. They did stick -- installed_plugins.json has no
locking, every `claude` process holds a full copy, and a concurrent session writing it back
restored the deleted records. Not a daemon regenerating state; a lost update. Hand-edit only
with other sessions closed, and prefer the CLI.
CONFIRMED FIX, applied 2026-08-06 to context7 (local) and security-guidance (local): patch
the record's projectPath from `c:` to `C:`, THEN run `claude plugin uninstall X --scope
local` from the target repo. Both succeeded on the first attempt after the patch, having
failed repeatedly before it. Patch the casing at removal time, not before -- repointing a
live plugin's projectPath is only safe when the next step deletes the record anyway.
STILL LOWERCASE and deliberately untouched: frontend-design (project, klondike_gui). It is
legitimately project-scoped and wanted there, so it costs this repo nothing and needs no
removal. Patch it only if it ever has to come out.

$comment: Budget for this repo's own skills/*/SKILL.md descriptions (description + when_to_use).
perSkillMaxChars is the platform cap: a listing entry is truncated at 1536 chars
(code.claude.com/docs/en/skills), so anything longer loses its trailing trigger keywords.
totalDescriptionChars is a RATCHET, not a target. It sits just above the measured baseline
so that unnoticed growth fails. The local surface is not what blew the budget -- one
third-party plugin was 4.5x the entire local skill set. Trimming the long descriptions is
worthwhile but separate; lower this number when that work happens.
RAISED 2026-08-11: ceiling 13000 -> 13375, measured baseline 12749 -> 13371 (+622).
Issue #139 asked for explicit boundary clauses on four confusable skill groups, so nine
descriptions each gained one clause naming the sibling to route to instead: git-manager /
using-git-worktrees / finishing-a-development-branch, librarian /
dispatching-parallel-agents, project-setup / infra-init, adherence-audit / review-workflow.
Raising the ceiling here is the 'deliberate, reviewable change' the test's own failure
message names as the sanctioned path -- it is not drift. Headroom is 4 chars on purpose:
a ceiling carrying slack is not a ratchet, and the next unplanned growth must fail at once.
RAISED AGAIN 2026-08-11: ceiling 13375 -> 13441, measured baseline 13371 -> 13437 (+66).
The three install-vetting gate skills each gained the same 22-char clause naming their own
router (`vet-capability-fit`, `vet-reputation`, `vet-security`: '... funnel, run by
`vet-install`.'). Each said 'Gate N of the install-vetting funnel' without ever naming the
skill that runs the funnel, which left all three pairs unresolved under the overlapVerdicts
gate below. Same 4-char headroom, for the same reason.
RAISED AGAIN 2026-08-11: ceiling 13441 -> 13442, measured baseline 13437 -> 13438 (+1).
ADR-0014 retires the `plan-management:<mode>` colon notation. doc-author's description is the
only frontmatter site carrying it; the compact parenthetical form (`plan-management
(close-subplan, after ADR Promotion Scan)`) is the shortest rewrite that names the mode without
the colon. Raised deliberately in the same commit as the edit rather than shipping on the
remaining 4-char margin -- headroom stays 4, so the next unplanned growth still fails at once.
Resolution set and exemptions for scripts/reference-integrity.test.mjs.
Every entry is keyed by the thing being exempted and valued by the REASON it is
exempt. A missing or empty reason fails the schema check in skill-surface.test.mjs.
That requirement is the whole mechanism preventing this block from becoming the new
place dead references hide.
Resolution happens against COMMITTED STATE ONLY. CI runners are stock ubuntu/windows
images with no ~/.claude directory, so anything resolved by probing the local
filesystem is invisible to the gate that is supposed to enforce it. A machine-local
skill must be DECLARED here to be citable -- the same principle as plugins.expected.

$comment: Namespaces that ARE component namespaces but are not covered by plugins.expected,
plugins.removed, or the local skill set. A `ns:name` pair counts as a CITATION only
if `ns` appears in the union of those four sets; anything else is prose that happens
to contain a colon (file:line, node:test, type:feat, justify-content:center).
This list is POSITIVE by design. The inverse -- 'ns is not a known skill or plugin,
therefore dead' -- is not provable: measured over this corpus it yields 48 findings
of which 17 are real. A positive declaration is diffable and cannot silently widen.
knownNamespaces.elements-of-style: Permanently declared dead. Never a local skill and never in plugins.expected or plugins.removed, so any `elements-of-style:` citation resolves to nothing. The one occurrence (skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md:295) is removed in the same slice that adds this entry; the entry STAYS afterwards as a recurrence guard, exactly as plugins.removed guards a deleted plugin. Do not delete it when the citation goes -- that would let the reference silently return.

$comment: Declared exemptions for zero-inbound-edge nodes in the component graph.
A node with no inbound edge is either a defect -- something should cite it but doesn't --
or an entry point by design -- nothing is supposed to dispatch it. This block records the
latter. Every entry is keyed by the orphaned component and valued by the REASON it is
exempt. A missing or empty reason fails the schema check in skill-surface.test.mjs -- the
same mechanism that guards the references block above.
Checked in both directions by the graph invariant that consumes this block: every
zero-inbound-edge node must appear here, and every name declared here must still have
zero inbound edges -- a stale exemption fails exactly like a missing one.

$comment: Declared exemptions from the ADR-0003 documentation-coverage oracle, enforced by
scripts/graph-integrity.test.mjs. Every component in the generated inventory must be
named in >= 1 docs/explanation/ doc, or be recorded here catalog-only with a stated
reason for having no narrative home. Every entry is keyed by the exempted component and
valued by the REASON it is exempt. A missing or empty reason fails the schema check in
skill-surface.test.mjs -- the same mechanism that guards the references and entryPoints
blocks above. Checked in both directions by graph-integrity.test.mjs: every entry must
still name a real component with no docs/explanation/ mention -- a stale exemption fails
exactly like a missing one.
This answers a different question than entryPoints: entryPoints is 'nothing cites this
in the graph, by design'; catalogOnly is 'no docs/explanation/ doc describes this, by
design'. A node can legitimately be in one, both, or neither -- do not conflate them.
docs/_coverage-audit.md remains the narrative record of the original 76-component audit;
this block is the checked one that is re-verified on every test run.
catalogOnly.cspell: A self-contained tooling-hygiene rule (spellcheck false-positive word-list maintenance). It has no subsystem narrative — forcing it into a feature explainer would be artificial. Fully described by its own file + its `component-inventory.md` line. The instruction-loading-layer model that governs all rules is explained in `docs/explanation/architecture.md`.

$comment: Recorded confusability verdicts for the skill-description candidate band, enforced by
scripts/graph-integrity.overlap.test.mjs. Structurally UNLIKE references / entryPoints /
catalogOnly: those are keyed by a single component name and valued by a reason string;
this is keyed by a PAIR (`skill-a|skill-b`, names sorted, matching the key form the band
computation builds) and valued by { verdict, reason }.
The band is every skill pair whose deduped, stop-worded description tokens exceed a
declared Jaccard threshold. BAND MEMBERSHIP IS NOT A DEFECT -- it means two descriptions
read similarly enough that a reader could plausibly confuse them. What fails is a band
member with NO VERDICT here. The already-disambiguated pairs sit in the band and pass.
Two verdicts, deliberately not three:
boundary -- one description names the other skill, or both name a common router. The
gate RE-VERIFIES this against the description text; the text is the proof,
so there is no evidence field to fill in and none to be trusted. This is
the only verdict the gate can check, and checking it is what stops this
block becoming the new place unresolved overlap hides.
distinct -- the overlap is lexical coincidence. Accepted as declared; the reason must
name the shared terms that caused the false match.
A third `merge-candidate` state was designed and dropped: it would have carried a real
extra requirement (a link to a remediation finding) but ZERO band members would use it.
Building and red-state-testing a branch against no live data is speculative. Add it when
a real instance first needs it.
The threshold, the stop list and the tokenization live in the test file, next to the
sizing measurements that justify them -- they are the CONTRACT OF THE COMPUTATION, and
the band is not reproducible without them. This block records only the human judgments.

brainstorming|test-driven-development.reason: Lexical coincidence. The six shared tokens are `code`, `feature`, `first`, `implementation`, `refactor` and `writing` -- both descriptions are phrased around what to do BEFORE writing implementation code, which is a shared sentence shape, not a shared job. brainstorming explores solution approaches when the design is not obvious; test-driven-development governs the red-green-refactor order once the design is settled. Neither is an alternative route to the other's outcome, so a routing clause between them would be misinformation.

different-viewpoint|different-viewpoints.reason: different-viewpoints-lite opens by contrasting itself with different-viewpoint (`Unlike different-viewpoint (full sweep in order), this selects the 5 questions most likely to falsify...`), which is the whole distinction: full ordered sweep vs adversarial 5-question selection.

doc-author|doc-backfill.reason: doc-author names doc-backfill as one of its callers (`Invoked by ... /doc-backfill (whole-repo backfill)`). The pair is a caller/callee, not two ways to do one thing: doc-backfill decides WHICH docs a repo needs, doc-author writes one.

doc-author|docs-refresh.reason: Same caller/callee shape as doc-author|doc-backfill: doc-author names docs-refresh among the entry points that invoke it (`/docs-refresh feature|architecture (manual refresh)`). docs-refresh routes to a specialist; doc-author is one of the things it routes to.

executing-plans|subagent-driven-developm.reason: executing-plans carries an explicit routing clause (`For isolated fresh-subagent-per-task execution instead, use subagent-driven-development`). Both execute a written plan; the axis is single continuing context vs a fresh subagent per task, and the clause states it. One of the two calibration-anchor control pairs asserted by the gate.

git-manager|using-git-worktrees.reason: git-manager names using-git-worktrees in the ownership clause added for the confusable-git-skills fix (`Owns git operations; using-git-worktrees isolates a workspace first, finishing-a-development-branch integrates after`). Recorded as a boundary AND flagged in the test file's Step 9 finding: this trio is one domain with no shared name prefix, so the durable fix is namespacing, deferred to its own slice.

infra-init|project-setup.reason: infra-init routes first-time onboarding away from itself (`For first-time workflow onboarding, use project-setup`). Entered the band only as a RESULT of that clause -- the shared vocabulary it introduced raised the pair's similarity -- which is the anti-correlation this whole design is built around.

receiving-code-review|requesting-code-re.reason: receiving-code-review states the direction split explicitly (`Owns the 'respond to feedback' direction. For submitting work to be reviewed, use requesting-code-review`). The other calibration-anchor control pair asserted by the gate.

vet-capability-fit|vet-reputation.reason: Both name their router `vet-install` (`Gate N of the install-vetting funnel, run by vet-install`). Gates 2 and 1 answer different questions -- does it cover the need, and is it reputable -- and are ordered cheap-to-expensive by the router, so the router is the correct thing for a reader to be pointed at rather than each other.

vet-capability-fit|vet-security.reason: Same shared router as vet-capability-fit|vet-reputation: both name `vet-install`. Gate 2 (capability fit) vs Gate 3 (malware/CVE scan of the finalist).

vet-reputation|vet-security.reason: Same shared router as the other two vet-* pairs: both name `vet-install`. The highest-scoring pair in the band -- three sibling gates written to one template will always read alike -- and prefix-namespacing plus the router clause is the appropriate answer, not divergent prose.

writing-agents|writing-rules.reason: Both close with `Route through creating-tools, not directly`, so both name the same router. This is the router form the gate exists to accept: the right disambiguation points at the PARENT that dispatches by artifact type, not at a sibling authoring skill.

writing-agents|writing-skills.reason: Same `Route through creating-tools, not directly` clause in both. Highest-scoring of the three writing-* pairs; the family is prefix-namespaced, so a reader has a structural cue before reading either description.

writing-rules|writing-skills.reason: Same `Route through creating-tools, not directly` clause in both.
